scenarios.title: Kicks for the Hospital
scenarios.text: The club runs a kick-a-thon for the children's hospital, and you're the main event: a donation for every kick you make in an hour, with the patients watching from the sideline.

choices.label: Kick for the full hour
choices.result: A full hour without stopping. Your leg is jelly, and the total is the biggest the hospital has ever seen.

choices.label: Let the kids kick too
choices.result: Every kid gets a turn at the tee. The donations drop a little; the photos are the best of the year, and a nurse cries.

choices.label: Recruit the specialists
choices.result: The punter, the snapper and {holder} join in, and it turns into a contest. The crowd doubles, and so does the total.

scenarios.title: The Night Before Your Debut
scenarios.text: The night before your first regular-season game, and your phone won't stop: old coaches, cousins, a girl from your third-grade class. It's ten o'clock and you're wide awake.

choices.label: Phone off, early night
choices.result: The phone goes in a drawer at eight, and you read until you fall asleep. Nobody's message is more important than the morning.

choices.label: Answer two people
choices.result: {parent} and {best_friend}, nobody else. Their messages are the right ones, and you fall asleep with the phone on your chest.

choices.label: One more look at the plan
choices.result: The special teams plan, once more, then sleep. You walk in calm, and {coach} notices you're the only rookie not pacing.

scenarios.title: The Debut Week Interview
scenarios.text: The national broadcast crew wants five minutes with the rookie kicker before your first game. The producer has a clipboard and very specific ideas about your 'story'.

choices.label: Tell your real story
choices.result: Kicking in the backyard with {parent}, into a fence with a hole in it. It makes the broadcast, and {parent} watches it forty times.

choices.label: Keep it to football
choices.result: Football only, short and polite. The crew thanks you, nothing makes air, you're secretly glad, and {parent} is quietly disappointed for a day.

choices.label: Talk about the unit
choices.result: The snapper and {holder}, mostly, and how a kick is really three people. The specialists' chat is very happy, and {holder} pretends to be annoyed.

scenarios.title: The Team Photo
scenarios.text: The team photo, and you're in the back row next to a lineman who has never learned your name. He calls you 'kick' and asks which number you are.

choices.label: Introduce yourself again
choices.result: Your name, again, with a handshake. He laughs, and from then on he calls you by name, loudly, across the cafeteria.

choices.label: Smile for the flash
choices.result: A smile, the flash, and back to the locker room. You're the blurry one in the corner of the framed print.

choices.label: Organize a specialists' photo
choices.result: A specialists-only photo afterward, organized by you. It ends up framed in the facility hallway, and {holder} puts a copy on their fridge.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Payday Dinner
scenarios.text: Your rookie class decides to celebrate your first full paychecks together at a restaurant you can't pronounce, with a menu that doesn't have prices on it.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: The whole night, every course. The bill is absurd, the night is worth it, and you all take a photo with the chef.

choices.label: Suggest a cheaper place
choices.result: A cheaper place with the same view, you suggest. Half the class comes, the rest think you're cheap, and your half has more fun.

choices.label: Order in
choices.result: Takeout, alone, on the couch. Your account is happier than you are, and you see the photos the next morning.

scenarios.title: The Trainer's Warning
scenarios.text: A trainer stops you in the hallway and quietly warns you about the supplements a veteran keeps recommending to the rookies. Some of them, the trainer says, aren't on the approved list.

choices.label: Make a rule for yourself
choices.result: A rule, made that night: nothing the club hasn't approved, ever. You sleep better knowing it, and the trainer notices.

choices.label: Warn the other rookies
choices.result: The other rookies hear exactly what the trainer said, from you. Two of them throw theirs out that night, and one of them thanks you a year later.

choices.label: Let the veterans sort it out
choices.result: Not your business, you decide, and you never ask what the others are taking. You're fine. You're not sure all of them are.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Talks Too Much
scenarios.text: A rookie in your class keeps posting locker-room jokes online: who fell asleep in meetings, who cried at a movie on the plane. The veterans are getting angry, and they've noticed you sit with him.

choices.label: Talk to him privately
choices.result: A quiet word in the parking lot. He genuinely didn't know it was a big deal, deletes four posts on the spot and buys the veterans breakfast on Friday.

choices.label: Let a veteran handle it
choices.result: A veteran you trust hears it from you, and handles it better than you could have: one sentence in the weight room, and the posts stop.

choices.label: Let him learn the hard way
choices.result: Not your fight, you decide. The veterans handle it loudly, with a whole-team meeting, and the rookie doesn't speak to anyone for a week.

scenarios.title: The Specialist Meeting Room
scenarios.text: The specialists' meeting room is the size of a closet, with a broken projector, one working outlet and a mop bucket nobody has moved since September. Three of you share it every morning.

choices.label: Ask for a real room
choices.result: The operations staff gets a polite, specific request from you, with a floor plan. You get a real room by Monday, and the punter calls you a hero for a month.

choices.label: Make the closet great
choices.result: Snacks, a better extension cord and a lamp from home. The closet becomes the best room in the building, and the linebackers start asking to visit.

choices.label: Use the film room at night
choices.result: The main film room after hours, empty and quiet. You learn more alone there in a week than in a month of closet mornings.

scenarios.title: The Wrong Bus
scenarios.text: After a road practice you get on the wrong team bus, fall asleep, and wake up alone at the airport cargo terminal. Your phone is at four percent, and the team plane leaves in three hours.

choices.label: Post it in the group chat
choices.result: A photo of you alone at the cargo terminal goes to the group chat. The nickname 'Freight' sticks for a whole season, and you secretly love it.

choices.label: Call the travel staff
choices.result: Four percent is enough for one call to the travel staff, who send a car. You're back before anyone notices, except the travel director, who never forgets.

choices.label: Wait with a book
choices.result: Three hours with a paperback and a vending-machine dinner until the team arrives. Nobody believes your story, and the snapper still brings it up.

scenarios.title: Your First Billboard
scenarios.text: Your face goes up on a billboard by the highway for a local bank, forty feet wide, smiling a smile you don't remember making. You drive past it twice on the way to practice.

choices.label: Send a photo home
choices.result: A photo from the shoulder goes to {parent}, who drives three hours just to stand under it and take his own. He frames it for the hallway.

choices.label: Take a different road
choices.result: A different route to practice, every day. It's too strange to look at your own face that big, and you feel silly about it.

choices.label: Earn the billboard
choices.result: Billboards are for people who've earned them, you decide, and you kick an extra hundred balls that week to start.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Retirement Party
scenarios.text: A veteran you barely know is retiring after eleven seasons, and the whole team is expected at the party in a hotel ballroom. He has never said more than three words to you.

choices.label: Listen to the stories
choices.result: An evening of stories at the back table: the old coaches, the cut days, the plays nobody filmed. You learn more about the league in one night than in a month.

choices.label: Stop by briefly
choices.result: Half an hour, a handshake and a congratulations. He remembers your name, which surprises you both, and you're home by nine.

choices.label: Toast for the rookies
choices.result: A short toast on behalf of the rookies, written on a napkin at the table. The veteran shakes your hand for a long time afterward.

scenarios.title: The Mentor Who Leaves
scenarios.text: The veteran who took you under his wing in camp is traded on a Tuesday night. By Wednesday morning his locker is empty and his name is off the parking spot.

choices.label: Help him pack the car
choices.result: His car, packed at midnight, with you carrying the heavy boxes. You keep in touch every week, and he texts you after every one of your games.

choices.label: Take his place in the room
choices.result: For the next rookie, you start doing exactly what he did for you: lunch, film, the long talks. It's the best way to thank him.

choices.label: Kick the sting out
choices.result: The sting goes into extra work that afternoon. It helps, a little, and you still look at his empty locker every morning.

scenarios.title: The Agent's Other Rookies
scenarios.text: Your agent has four rookie clients, and from how long your calls take to be returned, you can tell you're fourth. The last text you got was a thumbs-up to a question.

choices.label: Ask for a written plan
choices.result: A written plan and a monthly call, requested politely and firmly. You get both, and your agent starts calling first.

choices.label: Be impossible to ignore
choices.result: The client who's impossible to ignore, that's the plan, and you kick like it all month. Your agent calls in October to say the club asked about you.

choices.label: Let it ride
choices.result: Rookie contracts are fixed anyway, you reason, and let it ride. It's fine for now, and you wonder about next year.
